title: Capacity cutover playbook — dry run log
content:
Meeting: Capacity cutover playbook — dry run
Date: 2026-03-09
Organizer: Asha Menon
Attendees: Asha Menon, Ethan Park, Priya Shah, Omar Khalid, Sofie Andersson, Lina Zhou (observability)
Objective: Run the staged capacity cutover playbook against staging clusters (eu-west-1 / us-west-2) and validate rollback, routing rules, and SLO guardrails. Capture deviations and decide follow-up changes to the playbook before prod cutover.

Agenda:
- Quick sync on goals and metrics to watch (2 min)
- Execute dry-run steps 1–8 as written in playbook (simulate traffic ramps) (40 min)
- Observe telemetry and incident simulation hooks (10 min)
- Triage discrepancies and document action items (20 min)

Summary of actions performed (dry run):
1) Baseline capture: 15m steady-state traffic (500 rps synthetic mix; 60% short seq, 30% medium, 10% long). Observability snapshot saved as baseline (obs-snap-20260309-01).
2) Step 1: Gradual routing shift to new capacity pool (10% increments every 3 min). Automated router applied policy 'cutover-staged-v1' via feature-flag.
3) Step 2: Enable prefix KV cache warmup for new slots after first 30% ramp. Warmup finished in ~7m.
4) Step 3: Induce synthetic latency spike on old pool to validate fallback (introduced 200ms artificial delay on old-hosts). Confirmed automatic fallback triggered when p95 exceeded 300ms for 2 consecutive windows.
5) Step 4: Simulated instance termination (preempt) in new pool to validate session migration and retry semantics. One request observed as 502; retry logic recovered within 800ms.
6) Step 5: Increase to 80% routing; observed KV cache thrash on select shards for long sequences.
7) Step 6: Finalize to 100% routing and run post-cutover smoke checks (token accounting, model checksum, per-route quotas).
8) Rollback executed after smoke failures detected (see details).

Telemetry observations (high-level):
- Latency:
  - Baseline p50/p95/p99: 45ms / 120ms / 420ms
  - During 80% ramp: p95 rose to 260ms on eu-west-1 (acceptable per soft guardrail but above target).
  - During induced old-pool delay: fallback latency spike recovered within 1.1s but tail remained elevated for ~6 minutes.
- Errors:
  - One flake in session migration produced a 502 returned to client; retry path handled subsequent attempts. Root cause: race in session-affinity table update (ticket INF-7899).
- Resource utilization:
  - New capacity pool GPU memory at 78% during warmup; CPU on control-plane pods briefly hit 85% during routing scale event.
- KV cache behavior:
  - Warmup completed but hit increased eviction churn for long-seq workloads when ramp crossed 70%. Eviction latency contributed ~40ms to overall token latency for affected requests.
- Observability gaps noted:
  - No explicit per-tenant cache hit metric exposed in the default dash; had to join traces to infer. Create metric (action item).

Deviations from playbook and failure modes:
- Playbook assumes warmup will finish under 5m for target model shard ratio; observed 7m in staging due to background snapshot syncs. Implication: extend warmup window or pre-warm more aggressively.
- Fallback trigger threshold too sensitive for the synthetic delay scenario — it caused a brief thrash between pools before stable fallback. Consider hysteresis (min duration 60s and increase p95 threshold by 20%) to avoid oscillation.
- Session-affinity update race discovered under simulated `preempt` event (INF-7899). Severity: medium (single request failed, automatic retry worked). Recommend backport fix to session placement shim.

Decision log (explicit decisions made during meeting):
- D1: Warmup window increased from 5m to 8m for models >10B in staging and prod (agreed). Owner: Ethan Park. Due: 2026-03-16.
- D2: Introduce a 60s hysteresis window before fallback re-evaluation to prevent oscillation. Also add a 20% buffer to p95 threshold for cutover routing decisions. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-03-15.
- D3: Add a pre-cutover check that validates control-plane CPU usage <75% for last 10m; if not, abort cutover and alert SRE. Owner: Sofie Andersson. Due: 2026-03-13.
- D4: Add explicit per-tenant cache hit ratio metric to the observability schema. Owner: Lina Zhou. Due: 2026-03-14.

Action items (triaged and owners):
- A1: Patch session-affinity update race (INF-7899). Owner: Omar Khalid. ETA: 2026-03-12. Priority: P0 for cutover.
- A2: Update cutover playbook to reflect extended warmup, hysteresis, CPU pre-checks, and rollback checklist. Owner: Asha Menon. ETA: 2026-03-11. Priority: P0.
- A3: Implement per-tenant cache hit metric and add to default routing dashboard. Owner: Lina Zhou. ETA: 2026-03-14. Priority: P1.
- A4: Run two more dry runs targeting mixed long-seq heavy workloads and regional failover scenarios (schedule: 2026-03-11 and 2026-03-13). Owner: Ethan Park.
- A5: Create runbook snippet for manual velocity kill (how to clamp routing to 30% quickly) and add to incident playbook. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-12.

Rollback and mitigation notes (short form):
- Immediate rollback criteria: any of the smoke checks failing (token mismatch, model checksum), sustained p95 > 500ms for >5m, or >2% client-visible error increase for 10m.
- Rollback steps executed in dry run: revert router policy to 'cutover-pre' (automated flag rollback), flush warm cache on new pool, reattach sessions where needed, and hold traffic on old pool. Rollback completed in 4.3 minutes in staging.
- Manual mitigation: if rollback doesn't stabilize, scale up old pool by 30% and route 100% while SRE investigates.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Do we prefer conservative hysteresis that may delay fallback (longer healing) vs. aggressive fallback that may oscillate? Consensus: prefer conservative for customer-facing services.
- Q2: Should warmup be decoupled from routing percentage (i.e., only advance routing when cache hit ratio > X)? Proposal: gating advance on cache-hit > 65% for long seq traffic. Need to prototype.
- Q3: Is the current observability retention for routing traces sufficient for post-cutover forensics? Lina to propose retention increase if needed.

Appendix / artifacts captured during dry run:
- obs-snap-20260309-01 (baseline)/obs-snap-20260309-02 (80%-ramp)/obs-snap-20260309-03 (post-rollback)
- perf-trace: github.com/redwood-inference/trace-archive/2026-03-09-cutover
- screen recordings: internal-drive/recs/cutover-dryrun-20260309.mp4

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- We should bake hysteresis into router policy primitives, not as ad-hoc in scripts — primitives -> easier to test.
- Consider a 'preheat' job that runs during low traffic windows to pre-populate long-seq KV keys across new pool. Could reduce warmup time and eviction churn.
- Keep P0 fixes scoped small; the session-affinity fix looks small but needs careful regression tests.

Next steps: owners to update playbook and run two follow-up dry runs; reconvene after the second dry run for final sign-off for prod cutover.

Document history: created 2026-03-09 by Asha Menon; updated 2026-03-12 after triage meeting and adding decisions/actions.
